## Example 1: Spatiotemporal patterns of the *Picea* genus across North America since the LGM

The first example demonstrates how to retrieve data for the genus *Picea* across North America by selecting both modern and fossil pollen plot datasets, filtering samples by geographic boundaries and temporal range (0 to 15,000 yr BP), and harmonizing taxa to the genus level. The resulting dataset allows users to study spatiotemporal patterns of *Picea* distribution over millennia. This can be accomplished by running the following code:

```{r}
#| label: Example 1 - North America Picea
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
data_na_plots_picea <-
  # Access the VegVault
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(path = "<path_to_VegVault>") %>%
  # Start by adding dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select both modern and paleo plot data
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "vegetation_plot",
      "fossil_pollen_archive"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to North America
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = c(22, 60),
    long_lim = c(-135, -60)
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # Limit the samples by age
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(0, 15e3)
  ) %>%
  # Add taxa & classify all data to a genus level
  vaultkeepr::get_taxa(classify_to = "genus") %>%
  # Extract only Picea data
  vaultkeepr::select_taxa_by_name(sel_taxa = "Picea") %>%
  vaultkeepr::extract_data()
```

Now, we plot the presence of *Picea* in each 2500-year bin. 

```{r}
#| label: Example 1 - North America Picea - real
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
plan_na_plots_picea <-
  # Access the VegVault
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(
    path = path_to_vegvault # [config]
  ) %>%
  # Start by adding dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select both modern and paleo plot data
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "vegetation_plot",
      "fossil_pollen_archive"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to North America
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = y_lim_na,
    long_lim = x_lim_na,
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # Limit the samples by age
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(0, 12e3),
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # Add taxa & classify all data to a genus level
  vaultkeepr::get_taxa(
    classify_to = "genus"
  ) %>%
  # Extract only Picea data
  vaultkeepr::select_taxa_by_name(sel_taxa = "Picea")

data_na_plots_picea_raw <-
  vaultkeepr::extract_data(
    plan_na_plots_picea,
    return_raw_data = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  )

# The extraction leaves the connection of the plan open
DBI::dbDisconnect(purrr::chuck(plan_na_plots_picea, "db_con"))

data_na_plots_picea <-
  data_na_plots_picea_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    dataset_type %in% c("vegetation_plot", "fossil_pollen_archive")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    dataset_id, dataset_type, coord_long, coord_lat, sample_id, age,
    taxon_name, value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    taxon_name == "Picea",
    value > 0
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    dataset_id, dataset_type, coord_long, coord_lat, age
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_bin = (floor(age / time_step) * time_step) / 1e3
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_bin_class = dplyr::case_when(
      .default = paste("paleo:", age_bin, "ka cal yr BP"),
      dataset_type == "vegetation_plot" ~ "contemporary",
    ),
    age_bin_class = factor(age_bin_class,
      levels = c(
        "contemporary",
        paste(
          "paleo:",
          seq(0, 10, time_step / 1e3),
          "ka cal yr BP"
        )
      )
    ),
    dataset_type = stringr::str_replace_all(
      dataset_type,
      "_",
      " "
    )
  )


fig_na_plots_picea <-
  data_na_plots_picea %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long,
      y = coord_lat
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_quickmap(
    xlim = x_lim_na,
    ylim = y_lim_na
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    subtitle = "Each point is a presence of the Picea genus at a given time",
    y = "Latitude",
    x = "Longitude",
    col = "Dataset type",
    caption = "Small black dots mark the exact positions."
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      col_purple_light,
      col_green_light
    ),
    name = "Dataset type",
    labels = c(
      "fossil pollen archive",
      "vegetation plot"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(15, 16),
    name = "Dataset type",
    labels = c(
      "fossil pollen archive",
      "vegetation plot"
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom"
  ) +
  # Country outlines; ggplot2::borders() fails in facetted plots
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = col_beige_dark, # [config]
    col_line = NA,
    linewidth = line_size # [config]
  ) +
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = NA,
    col_line = col_blue_light, # [config]
    linewidth = line_size # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      col = dataset_type,
      shape = dataset_type
    ),
    size = point_size # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    size = 0.1,
    col = col_black # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(
    ~age_bin_class
  )

ggplot2::ggsave(
  here::here("Outputs/Figures/website/DB_example/fig_na_plots_picea.png"),
  plot = fig_na_plots_picea,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  bg = col_beige_light # [config]
)

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("Outputs/Figures/website/DB_example/fig_na_plots_picea.png"))

```

## Example 2: Joined Species Distribution model for all vegetation within Czechia

In the second example, the project aims to do species distribution modelling for plant taxa in the Czech Republic based on contemporary vegetation plot data and mean annual temperature. The code includes selecting datasets and extracting relevant abiotic data as followed:

```{r}
#| label: Example 2 - CZ JSDM
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
data_cz_modern <-
  # Acess the VegVault file
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(path = "<path_to_VegVault>") %>%
  # Add the dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select modern plot data and climate
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "vegetation_plot",
      "gridpoints"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to Czech Republic
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = c(48.5, 51.1),
    long_lim = c(12, 18.9)
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # select only modern data
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(0, 0)
  ) %>%
  # Add abiotic data
  vaultkeepr::get_abiotic_data() %>%
  # Select only Mean Anual Temperature (bio1)
  vaultkeepr::select_abiotic_var_by_name(sel_var_name = "bio1") %>%
  # add taxa
  vaultkeepr::get_taxa() %>%
  vaultkeepr::extract_data()
```


Now we can simply plot both the climatic data and the plot vegetation data:

```{r}
#| label: Example 2 - CZ JSDM - real
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
# 1. Load data -----
plan_cz_jsdm <-
  # Acess the VegVault file
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(
    path = path_to_vegvault # [config]
  ) %>%
  # Add the dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select modern plot data and climate
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "vegetation_plot",
      "gridpoints"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to Czech Republic
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = y_lim_cz,
    long_lim = x_lim_cz,
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # select only modern data
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(0, 0),
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # Add abiotic data
  vaultkeepr::get_abiotic_data(verbose = FALSE) %>%
  # Select only Mean Anual Temperature (bio1)
  vaultkeepr::select_abiotic_var_by_name(sel_var_name = "bio1") %>%
  # add taxa
  vaultkeepr::get_taxa()

data_cz_jsdm_raw <-
  vaultkeepr::extract_data(
    plan_cz_jsdm,
    return_raw_data = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  )

# The extraction leaves the connection of the plan open
DBI::dbDisconnect(purrr::chuck(plan_cz_jsdm, "db_con"))

data_cz_climate <-
  data_cz_jsdm_raw %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    sample_id, sample_id_link, abiotic_variable_unit, abiotic_value
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na()

data_cz_plots <-
  data_cz_jsdm_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset_type == "vegetation_plot") %>%
  dplyr::filter(value > 0) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    sample_id, coord_long, coord_lat, taxon_id
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(sample_id, coord_long, coord_lat) %>%
  dplyr::count(name = "n_taxa") %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_taxa > 1)

data_cz_jsdm <-
  data_cz_plots %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    data_cz_climate,
    by = dplyr::join_by("sample_id" == "sample_id_link")
  )

fig_cz_jsdm <-
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long,
      y = coord_lat
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(12, 18.9),
    ylim = c(48.5, 51.1)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Longitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    fill = "MAT (\u00b0C)",
    size = "Species richness",
    subtitle = "Each point represents one vegetation plot",
    caption = "Small black dots mark the exact positions."
  ) +
  # A sequential scale that colour-blind readers can follow
  ggplot2::scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "cividis"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 5),
    range = c(
      0.2,
      point_size * 2 # [config]
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  ggplot2::guides(
    size = ggplot2::guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        shape = 19,
        col = col_green_light # [config]
      )
    )
  ) +
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = col_brown_light, # [config]
    col_line = NA,
    linewidth = line_size # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = seq(12, 18, 2),
    linewidth = line_size,
    colour = col_white
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = seq(48.5, 51, 0.5),
    linewidth = line_size,
    colour = col_white
  ) +
  build_world_borders_layer(
    col_fill = NA,
    col_line = col_blue_light, # [config]
    linewidth = line_size * 10 # [config]
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = data_cz_jsdm,
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = coord_long,
      y = coord_lat,
      fill = abiotic_value,
      size = n_taxa
    ),
    shape = 21,
    col = col_green_light
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = data_cz_jsdm,
    col = col_black, # [config]
    size = 0.1
  )

ggplot2::ggsave(
  here::here("Outputs/Figures/website/DB_example/fig_cz_jsdm.png"),
  plot = fig_cz_jsdm,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  bg = col_beige_light # [config]
)

knitr::include_graphics(here::here("Outputs/Figures/website/DB_example/fig_cz_jsdm.png"))
```

## Example 3: Patterns of plant height (CWM) for South and Central Latin America between 6-12 ka

The third example focuses on obtaining data to be able to reconstruct plant height for South and Central America between 6-12 ka cal yr BP  (thousand years before present). This example project showcases the integration of trait data with paleo-vegetation records to subsequently study historical vegetation dynamics and functional composition of plant communities:

```{r}
#| label: Example 3 - LA CWM
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
data_la_traits <-
  # Acess the VegVault file
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(path = "<path_to_VegVault>") %>%
  # Add the dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select modern plot data and climate
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "fossil_pollen_archive",
      "traits"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to South and Central America
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = c(-53, 28),
    long_lim = c(-110, -38),
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "fossil_pollen_archive",
      "traits"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # Limit to 6-12 ka yr BP
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(6e3, 12e3)
  ) %>%
  # add taxa & clasify all data to a genus level
  vaultkeepr::get_taxa(classify_to = "genus") %>%
  # add trait information & clasify all data to a genus level
  vaultkeepr::get_traits(classify_to = "genus") %>%
  # Only select the plant height (the trait domain is stored as "Plant heigh")
  vaultkeepr::select_traits_by_domain_name(sel_domain = "Plant heigh") %>%
  vaultkeepr::extract_data()
```

Now let's plot the overview of the data

```{r}
#| label: Example 3 - LA CWM - real
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
# 1. Load data -----
plan_la_traits <-
  # Acess the VegVault file
  vaultkeepr::open_vault(
    path = path_to_vegvault # [config]
  ) %>%
  # Add the dataset information
  vaultkeepr::get_datasets() %>%
  # Select modern plot data and climate
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_type(
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "fossil_pollen_archive",
      "traits"
    )
  ) %>%
  # Limit data to South and Central America
  vaultkeepr::select_dataset_by_geo(
    lat_lim = y_lim_la,
    long_lim = x_lim_la,
    sel_dataset_type = c(
      "fossil_pollen_archive",
      "traits"
    ),
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # Add samples
  vaultkeepr::get_samples() %>%
  # Limit to 6-12 ka yr BP
  vaultkeepr::select_samples_by_age(
    age_lim = c(6e3, 12e3),
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # add taxa & clasify all data to a genus level
  vaultkeepr::get_taxa(classify_to = "genus") %>%
  # add trait information & clasify all data to a genus level
  vaultkeepr::get_traits(
    classify_to = "genus",
    verbose = FALSE
  ) %>%
  # Only select the plant height
  vaultkeepr::select_traits_by_domain_name(
    sel_domain = "Plant heigh"
  )

data_la_traits_raw <-
  vaultkeepr::extract_data(
    plan_la_traits,
    return_raw_data = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  )

# The extraction leaves the connection of the plan open
DBI::dbDisconnect(purrr::chuck(plan_la_traits, "db_con"))

data_la_datasets <-
  data_la_traits_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset_type == "fossil_pollen_archive") %>%
  dplyr::distinct(dataset_id, sample_id, age) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(dataset_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    .groups = "drop",
    age_min = min(age),
    age_mean = mean(age),
    age_max = max(age)
  )

data_la_taxa <-
  data_la_traits_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    dataset_type %in% c("vegetation_plot", "fossil_pollen_archive")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    dataset_id, coord_long, coord_lat, sample_id, taxon_id, value
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(value > 0) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    dataset_id, sample_id, coord_long, coord_lat, taxon_id
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(dataset_id, sample_id, coord_long, coord_lat) %>%
  dplyr::count(name = "n_taxa") %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(n_taxa > 1)

data_la_height <-
  data_la_traits_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(dataset_type == "traits") %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(trait_value) %>%
  dplyr::select(taxon_id_trait, trait_value) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(taxon_id_trait) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_value = mean(trait_value)
  ) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(mean_value)

# 2. Build figure -----
fig_la_datasets <-
  data_la_datasets %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      y = reorder(dataset_id, -age_mean),
      yend = reorder(dataset_id, -age_mean),
      x = age_min,
      xend = age_max
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(
    linewidth = 1,
    col = col_purple_dark
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = age_min
    ),
    col = col_purple_light,
    size = point_size,
    shape = 15
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = age_max
    ),
    col = col_purple_light,
    size = point_size,
    shape = 15
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
    transform = "reverse",
    breaks = seq(12e3, 6e3, -2e3),
    labels = seq(12, 6, -2)
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "A: Records",
    x = "Age (ka cal yr BP)",
    y = "Records, sorted by mean age"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
    #  xlim = c(min(limits), max(limits))
  )

fig_la_taxa <-
  data_la_taxa %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = 1,
      y = n_taxa
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_violin(
    fill = col_blue_light,
    col = col_black
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.2,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = col_white,
    col = col_black
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "B: Genera",
    y = "Genera per sample"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(),
    breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 70),
    limits = c(0, 60)
  )

fig_la_height <-
  data_la_height %>%
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    mapping = ggplot2::aes(
      x = 1,
      y = mean_value
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_violin(
    fill = col_blue_dark,
    col = col_black
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.2,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    fill = col_white,
    col = col_black
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "C: Plant height",
    y = "Mean plant height per genus (m, pseudo-log scale)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(
    transform = scales::transform_pseudo_log(),
    labels = scales::label_number(),
    breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 70),
    limits = c(0, 80)
  )

path_fig_la_merge <-
  here::here("Outputs/Figures/website/DB_example/fig_la_merge.png")

# The three panels are measured and drawn on the device that writes the
#   file (the one ggsave() uses), not combined beforehand with cowplot:
#   cowplot measures the text on another device, where showtext is not
#   switched on, so the text is measured larger than it is drawn, which
#   leaves gaps around the axis titles
ragg::agg_png(
  filename = path_fig_la_merge,
  width = 10,
  height = 7,
  units = "in",
  res = 300,
  background = col_beige_light # [config]
)

# showtext starts on a new page, so the page comes before the panels are
#   measured
grid::grid.newpage()

grob_la_datasets <- ggplot2::ggplotGrob(fig_la_datasets)
grob_la_taxa <- ggplot2::ggplotGrob(fig_la_taxa)
grob_la_height <- ggplot2::ggplotGrob(fig_la_height)

# The panel of the records twice as wide as the other two
index_panel_datasets <-
  grob_la_datasets %>%
  purrr::chuck("layout") %>%
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(name, "^panel")) %>%
  dplyr::pull(l)

grob_la_datasets$widths[index_panel_datasets] <- grid::unit(2, "null")

# Side by side, with the tops and bottoms of the panels aligned
grob_la_merge <-
  base::cbind(
    grob_la_datasets,
    grob_la_taxa,
    grob_la_height,
    size = "max"
  )

grid::grid.draw(grob_la_merge)

invisible(grDevices::dev.off())

knitr::include_graphics(path_fig_la_merge)

```
